advanced-packaging-001.question: Which correctly describes chiplets?
choices: A technology that connects several small chips, divided by function, inside one package so they operate as one system
A technology that uses an entire wafer as a single chip
A technology that solders chips directly to the board without a package
advanced-packaging-001.explanation: Instead of putting every function on one large chip, the chiplet approach makes the compute section, I/O section and so on as separate small chips and connects them at high density inside a package. Small chips have high yield, and the best manufacturing process can be chosen for each function.

advanced-packaging-002.question: Which correctly describes a TSV (through-silicon via)?
choices: Lateral wiring formed only on the chip surface
An electrode that passes through the silicon substrate in the thickness direction, connecting stacked chips vertically
A solder ball used as an external package terminal
advanced-packaging-002.explanation: A TSV (Through-Silicon Via) is an electrode made by drilling a hole in the silicon substrate and filling it with conductor, electrically connecting the front and back of the substrate. It allows chips to be stacked with many connections over shorter distances than wire bonding, so it is used in 3D packaging and HBM.

advanced-packaging-003.question: Which correctly describes HBM (High Bandwidth Memory)?
choices: A slow memory using a single layer of flash memory
An SRAM cache built into the CPU chip
A memory that stacks several DRAM dies with TSVs and achieves high bandwidth with a very wide bus
advanced-packaging-003.explanation: HBM stacks several DRAM dies with TSVs and connects them to the processor through a very wide data bus of more than 1,000 lines, achieving high data transfer bandwidth. It is used in 2.5D packaging, placed beside the processor on a silicon interposer or similar, and is mounted on AI GPUs and other devices.

advanced-packaging-004.question: Which correctly describes the role of the silicon interposer used in 2.5D packaging?
choices: A heat sink for cooling chips
An intermediate substrate on which several chips are placed side by side and connected at high density with fine wiring
advanced-packaging-004.explanation: A silicon interposer is an intermediate silicon substrate with fine wiring made by semiconductor processes. Several chips, such as a processor and HBM, are placed side by side on it and connected with high-density wiring impossible on ordinary package substrates. The interposer connects to the package substrate through TSVs.

advanced-packaging-005.question: Which correctly describes hybrid bonding?
choices: A technology that enlarges solder bumps to improve connection reliability
A technology that connects using two wires at a time
A technology that directly bonds surfaces of copper electrodes and dielectric without bumps, enabling extremely dense connections
advanced-packaging-005.explanation: Hybrid bonding planarizes chip or wafer surfaces and directly bonds copper electrodes to each other and dielectric to dielectric at the same time. Because no solder bumps are used, connection pitch can be reduced to a few µm, and it is used in stacked image sensors and advanced chip stacking.

advanced-packaging-006.question: Which correctly describes a feature of fan-out wafer-level packaging (FOWLP)?
choices: Redistribution layers extend beyond the chip edges, so external terminals can be placed over an area larger than the chip
Connections are made only by wire bonding
The package is always smaller than the chip
advanced-packaging-006.explanation: In FOWLP, singulated chips are embedded in resin to form a reconstituted wafer, and redistribution layers extending beyond the chip edges are formed on it. It is thin without a substrate and can place many terminals, so it has been adopted for smartphone processors and similar devices.

advanced-packaging-007.question: Which industry-standard die-to-die interface aims to let chiplets from different companies connect to each other?
advanced-packaging-007.explanation: UCIe (Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express) is a standard for connecting chiplets within a package. A common standard makes it easier to combine chiplets made by different companies and on different processes, and is expected to broaden the use of chiplets.

advanced-packaging-008.question: Which is especially likely to be a challenge in 3D packaging, which stacks chips vertically?
choices: Chips are too light to secure
Temperature rise from heat generated by stacked chips, and removing that heat
advanced-packaging-008.explanation: 3D packaging has the advantage of shorter wiring, but because heat-generating chips are stacked, heat tends to build up and is hard to remove from the inner chips. Higher temperatures degrade performance and reliability, so thermal design is an important challenge.

advanced-packaging-009.question: Which correctly describes SiP (system in package)?
choices: Several chips and passive components are housed in one package to function as a system
All functions are integrated on one chip
A system is built with software alone
advanced-packaging-009.explanation: SiP builds a processor, memory, passive components and so on into one package to function as one system. Compared with an SoC, which integrates everything on one chip, it makes it easier to combine parts from different processes and can shorten development time.

advanced-packaging-010.question: In flip-chip connections, what is the main advantage of using copper pillars (Cu pillars) instead of solder balls?
choices: Bumps can be made larger to increase contact area
Bump pitch can be narrowed, and electrical and thermal conduction are also excellent
advanced-packaging-010.explanation: A Cu pillar bump is a copper pillar with a small amount of solder on its tip. Unlike solder balls, it does not melt and spread sideways, so the bump spacing (pitch) can be narrowed and many terminals placed. Copper conducts electricity and heat well, which also helps current capacity and heat dissipation.

advanced-packaging-011.question: What is the wiring layer called that is formed on a chip or wafer surface to route electrode positions to the positions of external terminals?
advanced-packaging-011.explanation: A redistribution layer (RDL) routes wiring from the chip's bond pads to where external terminals such as solder balls are to be placed. It is used in wafer-level packages, fan-out packages, interposers and more, and its wiring is becoming ever finer.

advanced-packaging-012.question: Which approach, instead of a large silicon interposer, embeds small pieces of silicon only at the chip-to-chip connection areas to achieve high-density wiring?
advanced-packaging-012.explanation: In the silicon bridge approach, small pieces of silicon covering only the connection areas between adjacent chips are embedded in the package substrate, and fine wiring on them connects the chips at high density. Because no large interposer is needed, large-area packaging becomes possible while keeping costs down.

advanced-packaging-013.question: Which is a correct advantage of glass substrates, being considered in place of organic materials for next-generation large package substrates?
choices: They are soft and easy to bend
They have high flatness and dimensional stability, making fine wiring easier to form
advanced-packaging-013.explanation: Glass has a flat surface and little dimensional change or warpage with temperature, so it is expected to make it easier to form fine wiring and dense through-vias even in large package substrates. Its application to large packages for AI and similar uses is being considered.

advanced-packaging-014.question: What is the technology called that mounts optical transceiver components close to switch ICs and the like in the same package, shortening electrical wiring to reduce power?
advanced-packaging-014.explanation: In data centers, as traffic grows, the power needed to transmit electrical signals over long distances has become a problem. CPO places optical transceiver components in the same package as switch ICs and the like, shortening the distance signals travel electrically and reducing power. It is one of the technologies integrating photonics and electronics.

advanced-packaging-015.question: Among hybrid bonding methods, which allows only chips judged good in test to be selected and bonded to the target wafer?
advanced-packaging-015.explanation: W2W bonding bonds entire wafers at once and is efficient, but defective chips get bonded to each other, and good chips to defective ones. C2W bonding can select and bond only good singulated chips, giving a yield advantage, and chips of different sizes can be combined.

advanced-packaging-016.question: What are the bumps called, far smaller than ordinary solder balls, used to connect chips stacked with TSVs and to connect chips to interposers?
advanced-packaging-016.explanation: Microbumps are very small bumps arranged at pitches of a few tens of µm, used for the many connections between chips. They are used to stack HBM DRAM dies and to connect chips on interposers. When an even finer pitch is needed, hybrid bonding is used.

advanced-packaging-017.question: In AI GPUs, what is the main reason the GPU chip and HBM are placed side by side on one silicon interposer?
choices: To connect the chips over short distances with an extremely large number of wires, achieving very high memory bandwidth
advanced-packaging-017.explanation: HBM has more than 1,000 data lines, too many to route on an ordinary package substrate. Placing the GPU and HBM side by side on a silicon interposer, where fine wiring can be made, connects them over short distances with many wires, achieving the very high memory bandwidth AI computation needs.

advanced-packaging-018.question: In 3D NAND, which is a correct advantage of making the memory cell array and peripheral circuits on separate wafers and bonding them together?
choices: The manufacturing process always takes just one step
Each can be made with a process suited to it, and chip area can be reduced
advanced-packaging-018.explanation: Making the memory cell array and peripheral (CMOS) circuits on separate wafers with optimal processes and bonding them together puts the peripheral circuits under the memory cells, reducing chip area. Another advantage is that the peripheral circuits are not affected by the cell array's high-temperature steps.

advanced-packaging-019.question: What is the material called that is placed between a chip and a heat spreader to fill microscopic gaps and improve heat transfer?
advanced-packaging-019.explanation: Even when solids are stacked together, microscopic surface roughness leaves gaps that make heat hard to transfer. A TIM (Thermal Interface Material) fills these gaps to improve heat transfer; types include greases, sheets and metal-based materials. It is an important component for high-power processors.

advanced-packaging-020.question: What is the data transfer capacity that can be secured per unit length of chip edge called, emphasized as a performance metric for chiplet interconnects?
choices: Bandwidth density (transfer rate per unit length of chip edge)
advanced-packaging-020.explanation: Chiplets are usually connected through terminals arranged along their edges, so how much data can be transferred per 1 mm of edge length (bandwidth density) is an important metric. The energy needed to send one bit is also emphasized.

advanced-packaging-021.question: Which correctly describes the difference between 2.5D and 3D packaging?
choices: 2.5D places chips side by side on an intermediate substrate (such as an interposer), while 3D stacks chips vertically
2.5D stacks chips vertically, while 3D places chips side by side
There is no difference between 2.5D and 3D
advanced-packaging-021.explanation: 2.5D packaging places several chips side by side on an intermediate substrate such as a silicon interposer and connects them through the substrate's fine wiring. 3D packaging stacks chips vertically and connects them with TSVs or hybrid bonding. Structures combining the two are also used.

advanced-packaging-022.question: In HBM, what is the typical number of DRAM dies stacked in one stack?
advanced-packaging-022.explanation: In HBM, DRAM dies connected with TSVs are stacked 8, 12 or even 16 high and combined with a base die (logic die) at the bottom to form one stack. More layers increase capacity, but techniques for thinning dies and countermeasures for heat become necessary.

advanced-packaging-023.question: What is the concept called that integrates chips made with different manufacturing processes and materials into one package?
advanced-packaging-023.explanation: Heterogeneous integration uses advanced packaging to integrate chips made with different processes and materials — advanced-process logic, DRAM, analog, RF, photonic devices and more — into one system. It is attracting attention as a way to overcome the limits of monolithic integration, which builds everything on one chip.

advanced-packaging-024.question: Which correctly describes the typical TSV formation process?
choices: Form it simply by pouring in solder
Etch a hole by deep etching, form an insulating film and barrier layer, then fill with copper or similar
advanced-packaging-024.explanation: A TSV is made by etching a hole in silicon by deep etching (such as the Bosch process), forming an insulating film, barrier layer and seed layer on the inside of the hole, then filling it with copper or similar by plating. The wafer is then thinned from the back to expose the TSV tips.

advanced-packaging-025.question: What is the main aim of manufacturing packages all at once on large rectangular panels instead of round wafers?
choices: To increase the number processed at once and improve area utilization, lowering cost
advanced-packaging-025.explanation: Rectangular panels can hold square packages with less waste than round wafers and are easier to scale up, so many packages can be processed at once. Panel-level packaging is being developed as a way to lower costs, for fan-out packages and others.

advanced-packaging-026.question: To stack chips with TSVs, approximately how thin are wafers ground from the back?
advanced-packaging-026.explanation: Chips stacked with TSVs are thinned to a few tens of µm to keep hole depth down and reduce the total thickness after stacking. Thin wafers crack and warp easily, so techniques such as temporarily bonding them to a carrier substrate for processing are used.

advanced-packaging-027.question: Which correctly describes the benefits expected from using chiplets?
choices: They always become cheaper and faster in every case
The best process can be chosen for each function, small chips raise yield, and designs are easier to reuse
advanced-packaging-027.explanation: With chiplets, the best process can be chosen for each function — for example, an advanced process for parts that need high performance and a mature process for I/O and analog. Small chips have high yield, and the same chiplet can be reused in multiple products. On the other hand, chip-to-chip interconnect and packaging costs are added.

advanced-packaging-028.question: Which correctly describes the conditions required of the surfaces to be joined in hybrid bonding?
choices: Very high flatness and cleanliness at the nanometer level
A thick oil film on the surface
advanced-packaging-028.explanation: Because hybrid bonding directly joins surfaces of copper electrodes and dielectric without bumps, the bonding surfaces must be flat at the nanometer level and free of particles and contamination. Even a tiny particle can cause unbonded cavities (voids). CMP and cleaning technologies are important.

advanced-packaging-029.question: Which correctly describes the role of the base die (logic die) at the bottom of an HBM stack?
choices: It handles the interface between the stacked DRAM and the processor, as well as functions such as test
advanced-packaging-029.explanation: The HBM base die handles signal exchange between the stacked DRAM dies and the processor and also includes circuits for test and repair. Recently there has also been a move to make the base die with a logic process and give it more functions.

advanced-packaging-030.question: For high-power AI packages, which is a correct example of cooling methods being considered and introduced?
choices: Do nothing and wait for natural cooling
Liquid cooling, such as flowing liquid through cold plates or immersion cooling
advanced-packaging-030.explanation: AI GPUs and similar devices consume from several hundred W to more than 1 kW per package, so air cooling can no longer remove all the heat. Methods such as flowing coolant through cold plates and immersion cooling, which submerges entire servers in dielectric liquid, are being introduced.

advanced-packaging-031.question: Which is a basic advantage of 3D packaging, which stacks chips vertically?
choices: Interconnects between chips become shorter, enabling higher speed, lower power and a smaller footprint
The manufacturing process becomes simpler and cost always falls
advanced-packaging-031.explanation: Compared with placing chips side by side and connecting them through package substrate wiring, stacking them vertically makes the distance between chips very short. Signal delay and the power of charging and discharging wires shrink, many connections become easier to provide, and the footprint becomes smaller. On the other hand, heat tends to build up and processing becomes more complex.
choiceNotes: Correct. Shorter interconnects are the biggest advantage.
Stacking makes heat build up more easily.
Processing becomes more complex, and cost does not necessarily fall.

advanced-packaging-032.question: What is the problem called in which the speed of supplying data from memory cannot keep up with improvements in processor compute performance, limiting overall performance?
advanced-packaging-032.explanation: Processor compute performance has improved rapidly, but data transfer speed (bandwidth) to and from memory has grown more slowly, so compute units spend more time waiting for data. This is called the memory wall. It is especially severe in AI, which handles huge amounts of data, and advanced packaging that places HBM close to the processor is one countermeasure.
choiceNotes: Limits from heat are a different problem, called the power wall and the like.
Correct. It is the problem of memory bandwidth limiting performance.
Moore's law is an empirical rule about the growth in transistor count.

advanced-packaging-033.question: Which stacking method, long used in smartphone memory and elsewhere, stacks multiple chips slightly offset from one another and connects each to the substrate with wire bonding?
advanced-packaging-033.explanation: In a stacked MCP, thinned chips are stacked in a staircase offset or with spacers between them, and the electrodes at each chip's edge are connected to the substrate with fine metal wires. It needs no special processing like TSVs and is cheap to make, so it has been widely used in memory products stacking NAND flash and DRAM. However, its wires are long and limited in number, so TSVs or hybrid bonding are used where ultra-high bandwidth is needed.
choiceNotes: TSV stacking connects chips through electrodes that pass through the silicon.
Hybrid bonding joins electrodes directly to each other.
Correct. Each chip is connected by wire bonding.

advanced-packaging-034.question: In contrast to chiplets, what is the conventional approach called in which all the functions a system needs are built into one large chip?
advanced-packaging-034.explanation: Monolithic means "a single block of stone": all functions are built on one silicon chip. On-chip wiring connects everything, an advantage for performance and power, but yield falls as chips grow larger, and there is also a limit on the maximum area that can be exposed. Chiplets that split functions apart came into use for these reasons.
choiceNotes: Discrete refers to products such as single transistors and diodes.
Correct. It builds everything into one chip.
Hybrid is a general word for combining different things.

advanced-packaging-035.question: Advanced packaging steps that use front-end-like fine processing at the wafer level, such as forming TSVs and fine redistribution layers, sit between the front end and back end. What are they called?
advanced-packaging-035.explanation: In advanced packaging, TSV drilling and filling, fine redistribution wiring, bump formation, thinning and more are done on whole wafers with tools and techniques close to those of the front end. Because they fit neither the traditional front end (circuit formation) nor the back end (assembly and test), they are sometimes called the middle end.
choiceNotes: Correct. These are the steps between the front end and back end.
Upstream process is a term used in software development and the like for requirements definition and design.
Final process is not a common category.

advanced-packaging-036.question: Which TSMC 2.5D packaging technology is widely used to place AI GPUs and HBM side by side on a silicon interposer and connect them?
advanced-packaging-036.explanation: CoWoS (Chip on Wafer on Substrate) is a 2.5D packaging technology that mounts chips on a wafer-form interposer (chip on wafer) and then mounts that on a package substrate (on substrate). It is widely used to connect AI GPUs with HBM, and expanding its capacity became a major challenge as AI demand surged.
choiceNotes: InFO is TSMC's fan-out wafer-level packaging.
EMIB is Intel's silicon bridge technology.
Correct. It is the 2.5D packaging widely used to connect GPUs and HBM.

advanced-packaging-037.question: Which TSMC fan-out wafer-level packaging technology became widely known when it was adopted for a smartphone processor in 2016?
advanced-packaging-037.explanation: InFO is a fan-out packaging technology that forms redistribution layers on a reconstituted wafer with chips embedded in resin, making packages thin and small without a package substrate. Its adoption in 2016 for Apple's smartphone processors triggered the widespread use of fan-out advanced packaging.
choiceNotes: Correct. It is TSMC's fan-out packaging technology.
CoWoS is a 2.5D packaging technology using a silicon interposer.
HBM is stacked memory.

advanced-packaging-038.question: Which is a challenge of wafer-on-wafer (W2W) bonding, which bonds entire wafers together?
choices: Because good and bad chips cannot be paired selectively, the yield after stacking drops to the product of the individual yields
Wafers can be bonded even if their sizes differ
advanced-packaging-038.explanation: W2W bonding joins all chips at once and excels in throughput and alignment accuracy. But because it bonds regardless of which chips on the upper and lower wafers are good, bonding two wafers with 90% yield gives about 81% after stacking. It is therefore used for combinations of high-yield chips, such as memory cell arrays and peripheral circuits.
choiceNotes: W2W bonds with highly accurate alignment.
Correct. Bad chips cannot be excluded from the pairing.
Wafers of the same size are bonded together.

advanced-packaging-039.question: In 2.5D packaging, what is the main advantage of using an interposer made of redistribution layers (RDL) of organic dielectric and copper wiring instead of a silicon interposer?
choices: It can always form finer wiring than silicon
TSVs become unnecessary and no heat dissipation is needed at all
It keeps cost down more easily and makes large-area interposers easier to build
advanced-packaging-039.explanation: Organic RDL interposers do not use silicon wafer processing, so they keep cost down more easily, and they are flexible and easier to make large. On the other hand, their wiring fineness and density often fall short of silicon interposers, so they are chosen by application or combined with silicon bridges.
choiceNotes: Silicon interposers often have the finer wiring.
Heat dissipation does not become unnecessary.
Correct. Low cost and easy scaling up are the advantages.

advanced-packaging-040.question: Through the HBM3 generation, which is the data bus width per HBM stack?
advanced-packaging-040.explanation: Whereas a typical DDR DRAM module has a 64-bit data bus, HBM has a very wide 1024-bit bus per stack, achieving high bandwidth even though each line is not especially fast. That many wires cannot be routed on ordinary substrates, so high-density wiring such as a silicon interposer is required. The next generation, HBM4, widens it to 2048 bits.
choiceNotes: Correct. A very wide bus yields high bandwidth.
8 bits is a very narrow bus, the opposite of HBM's character.
64 bits is the bus width of a typical DDR module.

advanced-packaging-041.question: When a TSV wafer is thinned to tens of micrometers and processed, which technique temporarily attaches it to a support wafer (carrier) to prevent cracking and warpage?
advanced-packaging-041.explanation: A wafer thinned to tens of micrometers cracks easily on its own and warps significantly. It is therefore temporarily attached to a glass or silicon support wafer with adhesive or the like (temporary bonding), backside grinding and wiring are carried out, and it is then released by laser, heat or other means (debonding). It is an important technique for handling thin wafers safely.
choiceNotes: Wire bonding connects a chip to terminals with fine metal wires.
Correct. The wafer is handled while temporarily attached to a support wafer.
Reflow is the step of melting solder to make joints.

advanced-packaging-042.question: In fan-out wafer-level packaging, what is the wafer-like form called that is rebuilt by placing diced chips with spacing on a support and embedding them in resin?
advanced-packaging-042.explanation: In fan-out packaging, good chips are placed with spacing between them and surrounded with mold resin to rebuild a wafer shape, called a reconstituted wafer. Because redistribution layers can be formed on the resin extending beyond each chip, external terminals can be placed over an area larger than the chip.
choiceNotes: An SOI wafer has a thin silicon layer on an insulating film.
An epitaxial wafer has a single-crystal layer grown on its surface.
Correct. It is a wafer rebuilt by embedding chips in resin.

advanced-packaging-043.question: Which is a challenge of moving to chiplets?
choices: The area and power of interface circuits connecting chips, and the effort of assembly and testing, increase
Chips from different processes cannot be combined
advanced-packaging-043.explanation: With chiplets, connections that on-chip wiring handled in a monolithic design must pass through die-to-die interface circuits (PHYs), adding area, power and latency. Advanced packaging assembly, screening of good dies and post-stacking tests are also required. Adoption is therefore advancing in large chips where the benefits outweigh these costs.
choiceNotes: Correct. The burden of interfaces and assembly increases.
Splitting into smaller chips actually tends to raise yield.
Being able to combine chips from different processes is one of the advantages.

advanced-packaging-044.question: What is the main aim of products that stack a cache SRAM chip on top of a processor chip with hybrid bonding?
choices: To boost performance by placing a large cache close by without enlarging the processor
To raise the processor's supply voltage
advanced-packaging-044.explanation: A larger cache cuts memory accesses and raises performance, but SRAM takes a lot of area. Stacking an SRAM chip directly on top of the processor connects a large cache over a very short distance without enlarging the processor chip. Performance improves in uses where cache capacity matters, such as games.
choiceNotes: It is not for changing color.
Correct. Stacking puts a large cache close by.
It is not for raising the supply voltage.

advanced-packaging-045.question: Which method is used to make silicon interposers larger than the maximum area a lithography tool can expose at once (about 26 mm × 33 mm)?
choices: Exposing with wiring joined across the boundaries of multiple shots (stitching)
advanced-packaging-045.explanation: The area of a single exposure shot (the reticle size) is limited to about 26 mm × 33 mm. AI packages need interposers several times that size to hold a GPU and many HBM stacks. Stitching exposure, which precisely joins wiring across the boundaries of adjacent shots, is therefore used to make interposers larger than the reticle size.
choiceNotes: Correct. Shots are joined to expose a large area.
Enlarging lenses is not the solution; the exposure field is fixed by tool standards.
Wire bonding cannot achieve the fine wiring density of an interposer.

advanced-packaging-046.question: Which correctly explains how copper electrodes are joined to each other in copper-dielectric hybrid bonding?
choices: Solder is melted to connect the copper
The copper is stuck together with adhesive
The dielectric surfaces are bonded first, then heating expands the copper so the copper pads press together and join by diffusion
advanced-packaging-046.explanation: In hybrid bonding, planarized and activated dielectric (oxide or similar) surfaces are bonded near room temperature, and a subsequent anneal strengthens the dielectric bond. The copper pads are slightly recessed; thermal expansion during heating presses them together into close contact, and atomic diffusion merges them.
choiceNotes: Not using solder is a defining feature of hybrid bonding.
No adhesive is used.
Correct. It combines dielectric bonding with copper expansion from heating.

advanced-packaging-047.question: In classifying TSVs by when they are formed, which approach makes TSVs after forming transistors but before forming the multilayer interconnect?
advanced-packaging-047.explanation: By timing, TSVs are classified as via-first, made before transistors; via-middle, made after transistors and before the multilayer interconnect; and via-last, made after the interconnect or from the backside after thinning. Via-middle is widely used because it keeps copper TSVs away from high-temperature transistor steps while making them easy to connect to the wiring.
choiceNotes: Via-first forms them before transistors.
Correct. They are formed between transistor and interconnect formation.
Via-last forms them after the interconnect or after thinning.

advanced-packaging-048.question: Which pair of typical pitches (terminal spacing) for chip-to-chip connections is most appropriate?
choices: Microbumps about tens of micrometers; hybrid bonding 10 µm or less
Microbumps about several millimeters; hybrid bonding about 1 mm
advanced-packaging-048.explanation: Microbumps use solder and must avoid shorts from spreading solder, so their pitch is typically tens of micrometers (around 20 µm at the finest). Hybrid bonding, which uses no bumps, can go to 10 µm or below and even a few micrometers, providing orders of magnitude more connections in the same area.
choiceNotes: Correct. Hybrid bonding achieves pitches orders of magnitude finer.
Several millimeters is wider than ordinary solder balls.
100 µm or more is about the spacing of ordinary flip-chip bumps.

advanced-packaging-049.question: In manufacturing fan-out wafer-level packages, what is the problem called in which chips shift position because of resin flow or shrinkage during curing when they are encapsulated?
advanced-packaging-049.explanation: When making a reconstituted wafer, flow of the mold resin and shrinkage during curing and cooling can shift the placed chips slightly. This is called die shift. Large shifts misalign the chip electrodes with the redistribution layers formed later, so it is countered by material and process improvements and by position correction during exposure.
choiceNotes: Electromigration is the movement of metal atoms in wiring caused by current.
Latch-up is a high-current phenomenon caused by a parasitic thyristor.
Correct. It is chip misalignment during encapsulation.

advanced-packaging-050.question: What is the main reason for setting a keep-out zone around TSVs where no transistors are placed?
choices: Because stress from the difference in thermal expansion between copper and silicon changes the characteristics of nearby transistors
Because the area around TSVs cannot be exposed
advanced-packaging-050.explanation: Copper has a larger coefficient of thermal expansion than silicon, so temperature changes during manufacturing leave stress in the silicon around TSVs. Stress alters carrier mobility, shifting characteristics such as the current of nearby transistors. A keep-out zone of a set distance is therefore drawn around each TSV, and sensitive devices are not placed there.
choiceNotes: TSVs do not emit light.
Correct. Stress from the expansion mismatch changes characteristics.
The area around TSVs can be exposed.
